body:
Analysis of 158 external (GitHub Codex) review findings across ~79 wyrd PRs shows the dominant churn mechanism is *serialized review depth*: the external reviewer surfaces roughly one new, real, pre-existing finding per re-review round (extreme case: 13 rounds / 13 retriggers / 15 real findings on one PR). The harness currently stops at the draft PR and never sees any of it.

Proposal: a native pre-publish review stage in `publish.py`, between the T4 contribution gate passing and the deterministic git steps (branch/apply/commit/push/`gh pr create`):

1. Run N (configurable, default 3) parallel review passes over the bundle's full diff (`codex exec --sandbox read-only` via the existing family machinery), each carrying the role prompt and — with the rubric key from the companion issue — the target's rubric.
2. Union + dedup the findings; auto-drop classes the rubric explicitly rejects.
3. BUG-class findings feed the brief's carry-forward block and re-enter Do under the existing iterate budgets (`autoiterate.py` shape) — bounded, not open-ended.
4. Publish proceeds when a pass completes with every finding either fixed or recorded-rejected — a *triaged* fixpoint, not reviewer silence.

The wyrd instance runs the stopgap today: an instance-owned `scripts/review-branch` wired as a gating bundle-scoped T4 row in `[[gates.checks]]` (which `_t4_passes` already runs pre-push with zero engine change). That works, but the fix-loop half (step 3) can't be reached from a gate row — it needs the engine.
title: Pre-publish batched review stage: N parallel reviewer passes to a triaged fixpoint before the draft PR opens
